features.title: Local OTLP/HTTP receiver
features.summary: The Host listens on a loopback OTLP/HTTP port (4318 by default) and accepts POST /v1/traces in JSON and protobuf, gzip or deflate, from any OpenTelemetry exporter; spans are validated, bounded and stored with whole-trace retention. Plugin, external and both modes decide whether this receiver owns the port and whether it forwards to an external viewer. In plugin and both modes the receiver publishes its bound address in-process, so this Host's dshx spans and usage metrics arrive without OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT; traces_status and the panel carry a diagnosis of why nothing arrives (exporter elsewhere or off, port held, external mode).

configuration.constraints: plugin: this receiver owns the port; external: receiver off; both: store and forward to forwardUrl.
0 to 65535; 0 picks any free port. A port held by another process is reported and retried every 30 s.
A non-loopback host is refused unless this is on.
GenAI message, prompt and tool-payload attributes are stored as their size only.
1,000 to 1,000,000 spans; whole traces drop oldest first, alongside retentionHours (default 72).

failureModes: A body over 8 MiB, or one that inflates past 32 MiB, is rejected with 413/400 instead of being buffered.
A malformed protobuf or JSON body is rejected with 400 and nothing is stored.
A port held by another process (another collector, dsh-traces) leaves stored traces browsable and says so in the panel.
A non-loopback listen address is refused unless explicitly allowed.
A forward URL that points back at the receiver is ignored, so telemetry never loops.
GenAI content attributes are stored as their size unless redaction is turned off.
An unknown length-delimited protobuf field is skipped past its length prefix, so the next field still decodes.
An explicit OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT pointing elsewhere wins over the in-process receiver, and the panel says so with the supervisor-restart hint.

externalDependencies.boundary: OTLP/HTTP POST bodies (opentelemetry-proto v1 ExportTraceServiceRequest) from any exporter: LoongSuite (protobuf), dshx tracing (JSON), or a third-party SDK.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: Request bodies are produced by the official @opentelemetry/otlp-transformer serializers in unit tests and by a synthetic OTLP JSON payload in the browser journey.

features.title: Trace list and span waterfall
features.summary: A Traces panel lists stored traces newest first with filters (text, service, error status, minimum duration) kept across reloads; opening one shows a collapsible span waterfall on a time axis, colored by service with errors in red, and a side panel with the selected span's attributes, events and resource attributes, plus an Open thread link when a span carries dsh.session.id.
failureModes: A span whose parent never arrived is shown as a root rather than dropped.
A trace pruned while open reports that it is no longer stored.
A dsh.session.id for a thread this Host does not list is reported unavailable instead of opening anything.
A forged pagination cursor is rejected by the Host.

features.title: Per-thread Traces tab
features.summary: A Traces tab in the conversation view, after Trajectory, shows only the open thread's telemetry: traces with a span carrying its dsh.session.id (agent turn, model and tool spans and the plugin spans nested under them), a summary of spans, errors, model and tool calls, total and p50/p95 durations and gen_ai.usage token totals, a turn list that opens the span waterfall, and the thread's correlated logs. With nothing stored it says why, from the receiver's diagnosis.
failureModes: Token totals count model-call spans only, because the turn span repeats the same usage as its own totals.
A trace counts for the thread when any of its spans carries the thread's dsh.session.id, so plugin spans without the attribute still show under their turn.
On a Host older than the summary method the tab still lists the thread's traces and hides the summary.

externalDependencies.boundary: OTLP spans with GenAI semantic conventions (gen_ai.operation.name, gen_ai.usage.*) and dsh.session.id from an agent telemetry exporter such as LoongSuite.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: The otlp-session-turns scratch seed and the browser journey post synthetic LoongSuite-shaped OTLP JSON tagged with the open thread's id.

features.title: Log search with trace correlation
features.summary: The receiver also accepts POST /v1/logs (JSON or protobuf); the Logs tab searches stored records newest first by text, service, minimum severity and one attribute value, a record with a trace id opens its trace, and a span or trace opens only its own logs. GenAI content events keep only their body size unless redaction is turned off.

configuration.constraints: 1,000 to 1,000,000 records; the oldest go first, alongside retentionHours.

failureModes: A record without a time or observed time is rejected and counted.
A log whose trace was pruned still lists; opening it reports that the trace is no longer stored.
A forged logs cursor is rejected by the Host.

features.title: Service and operation overview, error groups
features.summary: A service strip and an Operations tab summarize span volume, error rate and p50/p95/p99 latency per service and operation over a chosen window; an Errors tab groups error spans by service, operation, error type and message shape with counts, first and last seen and a sample trace.
failureModes: Percentiles use the nearest-rank method, so a single sample is its own p50, p95 and p99.
Error messages that differ only by numbers fold into one group.

verification.testName: summarizes services and operations over a window

features.title: Service dependency map
features.summary: A Service map tab draws every service seen in the window as a box with span count, error rate and p95, and every cross-service parent/child call as an arrow with call count and p50, red when a call failed; picking a service filters the trace list by it.
failureModes: A call cycle between services still lays out and terminates.
Services with no cross-service calls are drawn without edges.

verification.testName: maps calls between services from cross-service parent and child spans
places callers left of callees by the longest call chain

features.title: Metric list with one chart per metric
features.summary: The receiver stores POST /v1/metrics (JSON or protobuf): gauges, sums, histograms, exponential histograms and summaries. The Metrics tab lists every metric per service with type, series count and last value, and charts the selected one per attribute set: gauges and sums as their value, cumulative counters as their increase between exports, distributions as their mean.

configuration.constraints: 1,000 to 2,000,000 data points; the oldest go first, alongside retentionHours.

failureModes: A metric without a known data type or a point without a time is rejected and counted.
A counter reset (the value drops) starts the increase again from the new value instead of charting a negative step.
More than 20 series are cut and the chart says how many were not shown.

verification.testName: decodes SDK metrics from protobuf into the same points as from JSON
keeps the metric type, temporality, value and attributes
lists metrics and charts a cumulative counter as its increase, per attribute set

features.title: Alert rules over stored telemetry
features.summary: Rules evaluated on the Host every minute over the stored spans: error rate, latency percentile, throughput, span count and span duration over a threshold, each with a service, span-name (exact or prefix*) and attribute filter, window, threshold, comparator and severity. A rule is ok or firing, resolves after two clear evaluations so a flapping signal fires once, and keeps a bounded history. A firing rule shows in the Alerts tab with its value, sample trace and threads, marks the Alerts tab and the panel with a red count and a banner, announces itself in an in-app banner (and a browser notification when allowed) wherever the user is, and marks the threads its spans carry unread through thread-sidebar. Rules can be created, edited, enabled, muted and deleted (with confirmation) in the tab or by agent tools. Four built-in rules ship with conservative thresholds.
failureModes: Error-rate and latency rules stay quiet below their minimum span count, so one failed span is not a 100% error rate.
A firing rule resolves only after two clear evaluations in a row, so a signal that swings every minute fires once.
A span counts in the window it ended in, so a 20-minute turn that started before the window still trips a duration rule.
A muted rule still evaluates and records its incident but announces nothing and marks no thread.
Disabling or deleting a firing rule resolves its incident instead of leaving it firing in history.
Without thread-sidebar the alert still fires and its event says why no thread was marked.
A Host older than alerts answers owner-missing: the tab says a restart loads it and the notifier stops polling.
Routine evaluations (no transition, no failure) and the alerts API dispatch spans are not stored, so the timer and the notifier poll never bury real traces.
An announced alert is claimed in localStorage, so several tabs announce it once, and a reload after a long absence announces nothing old.

externalDependencies.boundary: @dshfiles/thread-sidebar thread-sidebar-attention markUnread, called in process through its dshx contract.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: Unit tests pass a recording markThread port; the browser journey runs without thread-sidebar and asserts nothing about thread marks.

features.title: Boards and saved views
features.summary: A Boards tab breaks the window's spans down with built-in boards: slow tools (execute_tool by gen_ai.tool.name), failing plugins (dshx API dispatch by dshx.plugin.package), model latency by provider (chat spans with time to first token), jobs (by dsh.job.kind) and jj commands, each row with count, error rate and percentiles; a row opens the trace list filtered to its spans. A Views menu opens any board and saves or reapplies named views of the panel (tab, trace filters, log filters, window). traces_breakdown gives agents the same breakdowns. Not a dashboard builder.
reach: expect text "execute_tool spans by gen_ai.tool.name, slowest p95 first."
failureModes: Spans without the grouping attribute group as (not set) instead of disappearing.
An attribute key that could escape the SQLite JSON path is refused by the input schema.
Saved views are this browser's presentation state: they never leave localStorage and have no agent tool.
